answer: A slow trust ramp thwarts sybil attackers. Each agent carries a reputation score that rises after sustained, verified task completions, so a new identity starts at zero and earns high-value contracts only after weeks of honest service. Cloning multiplies identities, but each clone must re-climb the ramp, and fixed costs do not shrink, so returns spiral downward as clones multiply. A detected clone sends a ripple of downgrades through every identity sharing its infrastructure, collapsing whole farms. Like wind shaping a dune, trust accumulates grain by grain and cannot be fabricated.
